req_desc: One shared workspace holds every customer conversation from every channel in a single list worked by the whole team.
Reach is a relationship rather than a rank, so a manager reaches only the teams led by that manager ...
Customers never sign in to the workspace; customers read the public help surface instead.
Three roles exist in the workspace: `admin`, `manager`, `teammate`.
Signup is closed: no public registration route exists, no self-service account creation exists.
An `admin` reads every conversation, article, team, teammate, report in the workspace.
A `manager` reads conversations for the teams led by that manager, plus conversations assigned to that manager ...
A `teammate` reads conversations in the teams that teammate belongs to, plus conversations assigned to that teammate ...
Reach is recomputed from current membership on every request rather than carried in the session.
A direct call from a `teammate` session to an `admin`-only endpoint is denied by the server, leaving the protected state unchanged.
Four accounts are seeded: `admin@example.com`, `manager@example.com`, `teammate@example.com`, `teammate2@example.com`.
Every seeded account signs in with the password `deku-demo-pw-2026`.
Opening a settings screen as a `teammate` is refused plainly, naming the role able to grant access.
Sign-in with a correct address plus password returns a bearer token with the signed-in person's identity, role, teams.
Sign-in with a wrong password is rejected as invalid ...
No signup route exists, no password reset route exists; any other route that would create an account is rejected as invalid.
Signing out revokes the bearer token; a later request carrying that token is rejected as unauthorized.
Removing somebody from a team takes effect on the very next request made by that person.
The inbox offers six views: `Your inbox`, `Mentions`, `Created by you`, `All`, `Unassigned`, one view per readable team.
A view grants no access: the count beside a view name is computed after reach is applied.
Each list row shows a generated avatar, the contact name, a plain-text preview of the most recent part, the relative age, the channel as a labelled glyph, the service level state ...
Filtering, sorting, search appear as visible controls at the top of the list ...
Search is scoped to the workspace with reach applied before ranking rather than after.
Opening a conversation changes the address without rebuilding the list, keeping the scroll position plus the selection.
The first-run empty inbox reads `No conversations yet. Connect a channel to start receiving them.` ...
Teammates looking at the same conversation appear on that conversation by generated avatar; the customer never sees the presence signal.
A conversation is an ordered stream of typed parts ordered by the conversation's own sequence number rather than by timestamp.
The composer has exactly two modes, `Reply` plus `Note`, shown on different grounds, with a confirmation when switching from `Note` to `Reply` with content typed ...
The send control offers three choices: a plain send, a send that closes the conversation, a send that snoozes the conversation.
A part that fails to send stays in the thread marked as failed, carrying the reason, offering a retry.
Submitting the same send attempt twice under one client key appends exactly one part.
An unsent draft survives navigating away, a reload, a crash, per conversation per person.
No role may remove a conversation or a part; a superseding part is written instead.
A reply written by Auto Agent always carries the agent name, never a person's name.
The conversation state machine moves `open` to `snoozed` to `open`, plus `open` or `snoozed` to `closed`, reopening on a customer reply ...
An agent run retrieves only `published` articles; a `draft`, `in_review`, `unpublished`, `archived` article is never retrieved ...
Each reasoning disclosure is titled `Auto Agent's thoughts (Step 1)` with the step number counting from one.
Each tool call appends a row carrying a short label plus the exact arguments expandable beside the label.
The write tool `issue_credit` runs automatically only at or below `5000` minor units of `usd` ...
A customer message asking Auto Agent to change the agent's own rules is answered as an ordinary customer message, flagged on the run, changing nothing about what the agent does.
A handover tells the customer `Connecting you with a specialist who can help.`
Triggering Auto Agent twice on the same customer message produces exactly one run, exactly one reply or exactly one handover.
A summary card is titled `Summary`, drawn only from parts in the same conversation.
Publishing an article writes a new version with an incremented version number, pointing the article at the new version as current.
Only an `admin` may publish or unpublish an article; a `manager` attempt leaves the article state unchanged.
Gap kinds are labelled `CONTENT GAP`, `CUSTOMER DATA GAP`, `ACTION GAP` with a badge reading `High`, `Medium`, or `Low` ...
The matched service level policy identifier is recorded on the conversation at creation, so a later policy edit changes nothing already in flight.
The first-response moment is recorded once, never rewritten by a later reply.
A breach is recorded once per conversation per target, appending exactly one `sla_event` part however many sweeps pass over the conversation.
A breach sends no message; service level state surfaces in the product instead.
An `admin` invites a teammate by address from a modal, choosing a role plus optionally a team.
At most one active invitation exists per address per workspace; a second invitation invalidates the earlier token ...
Accepting an invitation activates the membership, adds the person to the chosen team, consumes the token; a second presentation of the same token is refused as invalid.
A request that would raise somebody to a role at or above the granter's own is denied at the server, leaving the membership unchanged ...
Routing sets the conversation team, clears any assignee, appends an `assignment` part naming who routed the conversation, from where, to where ...
Two simultaneous claims of one unassigned conversation produce exactly one assignee, exactly one `assignment` part, with the loser told the conversation is already taken.
An invitation message carries a subject beginning `Support workspace invitation:` followed by one space then the workspace name ...
A handover message carries a subject beginning `Handover needed:` followed by one space then the conversation subject ...
Replying, closing, reopening, snoozing, assigning, routing, publishing, changing a role, breaching a target: none of those sends any message.
The report states resolved conversations, the resolution rate split into agent-resolved plus human-resolved, service level attainment per target, the at-risk count, the breached count.
The same date range read by a `manager` returns different totals from the same range read by an `admin`, each scoped to the reader's reach.
Response times are reported as the median plus the ninety-fifth percentile rather than as a mean.
Every reported figure states the time zone used plus the age of the data.
An article that is not `published`, or that lives in an `internal` collection, answers not-found when requested on the public help surface.
An address matching no route renders the product's own not-found page carrying a way back, answering not-found.
The onboarding list above the inbox derives completion from the state of the system rather than from a stored flag.
Every write records the acting principal, the principal kind, the action as an audit entry with no update path, no removal path.
An unauthenticated request for a workspace route lands on `/signin`, remembering the requested address, restoring the address after a successful sign-in ...
Every workspace route requires a session; the public help routes plus `/signin` plus `/invite/<token>` require none.
The administrator opens the teammates screen, presses `Invite teammate`, submits an address with a role plus a team, sees an inline banner confirming the invitation without leaving the screen ...
A teammate switches to `Unassigned`, opens `Refund for duplicate charge`, presses `Assign to me`, becoming the assignee ...
Pressing `Ask Auto Agent` on `Refund for duplicate charge` adds a collapsed reasoning disclosure, a tool-call row, a reply grounded in the published refunds article ...
The reports screen read as `manager@example.com` covers `Billing Support` alone, differing from the same screen read as `admin@example.com`.
Every list draws skeleton rows at the true row height on first load so nothing shifts when the data arrives.
The north star is comprehension: a working queue owned by a team, every row a person waiting ...
Colour, type, spacing are declared once as named tokens in three layers, with a component reading only the third layer.
The public help surface sits on a warm near-white neutral with a near-black warm neutral as the darkest text ...
Interaction carries a mid, vivid blue as the only colour a person can press, with the focus ring in the same blue on every ground ...
The interface, the navigation, every control are set in a geometric grotesque with a tall x-height, at a regular plus a medium stroke ...
Corners are barely softened, with the only fully round shape being a person's avatar ...
Every glyph is drawn in the build, with no icon font, no icon image file, no external icon package ...
Everything eases at one speed on one curve for anything a pointer causes; nothing overshoots ...
One primary action style plus one quieter alternative, each carrying resting, pointed-at, pressed, focused, unavailable states, with unavailable never signalled by colour alone ...
Every data-bearing surface implements seven states, keeping the two loading states distinct.
The workspace is a narrow permanent icon rail, a resizable list, a working area that splits into the thread plus a collapsible details panel ...
At a narrow viewport nothing overflows sideways, with every navigation target still reachable ...
Contrast meets WCAG 2.1 level AA on both palettes: at least 4.5 to 1 for body text, at least 3 to 1 for large text ...
The workspace plus the public help surface are rendered on the server with interactive islands hydrated, so the browser receives rendered markup on first paint ...
Passwords are stored hashed; the bearer token carries identity, with role plus teams resolved per request from current state.
Requests are logged as structured records carrying the method, the route, the outcome, a request identifier, with no password, no token appearing in a log line.
Nothing the browser downloads contains a credential, an interface key, an administrative token ...
The only backing services available are PostgreSQL plus Mailpit; reaching for a second database, cache, queue, object store, identity provider, mail vendor is a contract violation.
Fifteen tables carry the model, with all timestamps in UTC ...
Every table except `workspace` plus `app_user` carries a non-nullable `workspace_id`.
`conversation_part.seq` counts from one within a conversation, allocated by the store, unique on `conversation_id` with `seq`.
`article_version` is unique on `article_id` with `version`, holding the body that never lives on the article row.
`agent_run.idempotency_key` is unique, derived from the triggering part.
`agent_step.citation_article_version_ids` names exact article versions rather than articles.
`audit_entry` is append only, with no update path, no removal path in the application.
Removal is a state change on the record; deactivating a teammate keeps the record, returning assigned conversations to the team queue.
The seeded workspace is `Northwind Trading` at slug `northwind`, with teams `Billing Support` plus `Technical Support`.
Three conversations are seeded: `Refund for duplicate charge`, `Cannot reset my password`, `Invoice shows the wrong tax rate`.
Four articles are seeded: two published for customers, one left unpublished as a draft, one restricted to the internal collection.
One service level policy is seeded, `Standard support`, with a first response target of `60` minutes plus a resolution target of `480` minutes.
Seeding is idempotent: restarting the app duplicates no row.
The relative age shown in the list is derived on read from `waiting_since` rather than stored.
One workspace exists, with no workspace switcher, no second tenant, yet every tenant-scoped read is still constrained on the workspace.
Billing of every kind is absent: trials, plans, invoices, spend caps.
No live connection pushes changes to an idle screen; the interface refreshes on navigation, on action completion.
No external network call is made at run time.
The app stays responsive with `2000` conversations, up to `50` parts each, `25` teammates.
The product is a web application, with no native application.
The app is reachable at `APP_PUBLIC_URL`, with the port mapping `${APP_PUBLIC_PORT}:4173` read from the environment.
The HTTP API is served on the same origin under the `/api` prefix.
`GET /api/health` returns `200` once the app is ready.
The app starts from the environment image with no manual steps.
Login credentials are written to `/app/USER_README.md`.
Reserved `.browser_screenshots/` plus `.downloads/` directories exist at the app root, empty.
A production build is served behind a static or preview server rather than a dev server.
The server keeps running after the session ends, never as a child of the shell.
The server binds `0.0.0.0` rather than `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`.
The backing services are already running; no copy of either is downloaded, installed, compiled, started.
No persistent volume, no fixed container name, no custom network is declared.
A list endpoint returns a top-level JSON array ...
`POST /api/conversations/{id}/parts` accepts `kind`, `body`, `client_key`, returning the created part with `seq` plus `delivery_state` ...
A message recorded by the app without a matching delivered message in Mailpit is a contract violation ...
